output.brief: The departures are concentrated in one place. Eight of the 11 associates on the Kestrel matter resigned, against 1 of the 13 who never worked on it. Every Kestrel associate was supervised by the new partner, Dorian Faulk, and he supervises nobody else. So the heavy workload and his supervision can't be told apart in the data. The survey complaints cover both: unsustainable weekends and humiliating late-night corrections. Pay, the firm-wide hours target and ordinary market movement don't fit. Other groups are stable, and the group's associates who weren't on Kestrel mostly stayed. I'm fairly sure the problem is tied to Kestrel, but unsure whether the cause is workload, supervision or both. Don't announce the £12k retention payment or close the review. It would miss the likely cause and cost £228k. Commission the roughly £9k confidential interviews now, run by an outsider and designed to separate supervision from workload. Four leavers have already agreed to take part. In the meantime, add matter and supervising-partner fields to attrition reporting. Hold off on moving supervision or paying £160k for contract reviewers until the interviews report.
